title: Supercurrent effect in a charge density wave intertwined superconductor
authors: Zhen Zhu, Wei Cheng, Dang Liu, Pengyu Hu, Yi Yang, Qiaoyan Yu, Shasha Xue, Ruijun Xi, Xingsen Chen, Jice Sun, Dandan Guan, Yaoyi Li, Shiyong Wang, Canhua Liu, Zhuan Xu, Xin Liu, Hao Zheng, Jinfeng Jia
abstract: The energy-momentum (E-k) dispersion of quasiparticles constitutes a fundamental concept in condensed matter systems. The ability to modify the E-k dispersion, exemplified by supercurrent-induced Doppler shifts of Bogoliubov quasiparticle spectra in superconductors, enables manipulation of various emergent quantum properties. However, investigations into the supercurrent effect on superconductors intertwined with charge orders remain scarce. Here, we report that the Meissner current, generated by the diamagnetic response to an applied in-plane magnetic field, can tailor Bogoliubov quasiparticle excitations at the precursor charge density wave (CDW) vectors. Our scanning tunneling spectroscopic imaging reveals a field-driven symmetry breaking of CDW modulations, specifically a C3v-to-Cs transition, in superconducting NbSe2. Model calculations suggest that the observed anisotropy originates from a selective Doppler-shift-induced E-k dispersion reconstruction. Furthermore, altering the field direction enables on-demand tuning of anisotropic CDW modulations and visualization of their momentum-space distribution. These results highlight a novel mechanism for controlling emergent electronic phases through momentum-space engineering.
summary: The research demonstrates that supercurrents flowing in a CDW-intertwined superconductor like $	ext{NbSe}_2$ can actively control the symmetry of the charge density wave. By applying an in-plane magnetic field, the system undergoes a measurable phase transition ($C_{3v}$ to $C_s$) observable through spectroscopic measurements and confirmed by theoretical modeling.
main_problem: The study investigates how supercurrents, specifically Meissner currents induced by an in-plane magnetic field, modify the electronic structure of superconductors that are intertwined with Charge Density Wave (CDW) order.
main_result: The applied supercurrent induces a Doppler shift on Bogoliubov quasiparticles, which drives a symmetry breaking transition in the CDW modulation from $C_{3v}$ to $C_s$ within the superconducting gap. This demonstrates momentum-space engineering control over emergent electronic phases.
method: The work combines experimental scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) measurements with theoretical modeling using tight-binding Hamiltonians and Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations incorporating Peierls substitution for supercurrent effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is superconducting $	ext{NbSe}_2$, which exhibits both s-wave superconductivity ($	ext{T}_{	ext{c}} \approx 7.2	ext{ K}$) and a $3	imes3$ CDW phase. The model incorporates hopping terms, the CDW potential, and pairing potentials into the BdG Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Bogoliubov quasiparticle spectra (coherence peaks), CDW modulation symmetry ($C_{3v}$ vs $C_s$), field-dependent peak intensities in Fourier Transforms of LDOS maps.
important_parameters: Applied magnetic field strength and direction ($\Gamma-	ext{M}, \Gamma-	ext{K}$ directions); energy window within the superconducting gap ($0.2-0.6 	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The authors assume that surface-vortex contributions are negligible during measurements, allowing the field effect to be attributed directly to the interplay between CDW order and Bogoliubov quasiparticles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate CDW modulation patterns (real space/FFT) under applied fields, showing symmetry breaking ($C_{3v} 	o C_s$) in the superconducting gap region. Band structures and constant-energy contours confirm the field dependence of the electronic states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by coupling CDW order to superconductivity via a Hamiltonian. It then presents experimental evidence using STS/STS mapping under varying magnetic fields, correlating observed symmetry breaking in the CDW modulation with Doppler shifts calculated from quasiparticle spectra and model calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides an example of how external electromagnetic fields can be used as a tool to selectively tune quantum ground states (CDW order) by coupling to superconducting excitations, which is highly relevant for designing novel electronic materials.
